lens: identity, provenance, authorization, privacy, freshness, state separation, and external-action authority

findings.observation: Each displayed contact point carries a source resource identifier and source label, but the current section-level View Source action opens the general source-review surface rather than targeting that exact source row.
findings.evidence: apps/backend/src/modules/people.ts contact_points projection; packages/contracts/src/resourceSchemas.ts RelationshipContactPointSchema; screenshots/contact-desktop.png
findings.user_impact: With several contact channels, a recruiter can see provenance exists but may spend extra effort locating the exact supporting source before trusting or correcting one field.
findings.recommendation: Make each contact point's provenance label a direct, scoped source-review action using source_resource_id, without revealing raw identity values in navigation or logs.
findings.verification: Open a person with three current contact points from different authorized resources; each provenance action must open only the matching governed resource and preserve masked display values.

strengths: User-authored profile text is visibly labeled as authored orientation and explicitly not evidence.
The backend projects only confirmed, unexpired contact hints with a non-deleted source and active source authorization; raw identity values are never returned.
Memory preserves proposed, contested, and confirmed status instead of promoting interpretation to confirmed person state.
The Agent create flow requires account-scoped identity checking and explicit recruiter confirmation; it states that it will not merge or contact anyone.
missing_evidence: A runtime revocation test proving an already open contact page removes a contact hint after source authorization is revoked.
A deletion and recovery test covering a contact point whose only governed source is deleted while the page is open.
open_questions: Should manually entered contact points use a distinct user-authored provenance object rather than the governed-source path?
